findings.title: The holdout NON-VACUOUS gate (the north-star anti-regression check) is DEAD CODE — never invoked from src/, and it is hard-coded pytest-only
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly as stated. The holdout step (extract_baseline_tests + run_holdout_tests) has ZERO functional callers in src/: the sole decide() call site (core.py:655) passes only grade+gate_results, the rung is driven off `prior` not decide's verdict, and the module is imported solely for the HoldoutResult type. It is also Python/pytest-bound by construction (.py + test_/_test.py discovery filter, hard-coded pytest invocation, pytest FAILED/ERROR summary parser), so even if wired it discovers and runs nothing for Go/Rust/Java. Double release-gate gap: inert today AND not language-portable.
findings.evidence: grep 'holdout_result\s*=' over src/ → 0 hits. grep run_holdout_tests/extract_baseline_tests over src/ → only the docstring + the 2 defs + __all__ in holdout.py itself; functional callers only in tests/test_tournament_holdout.py and tests/test_promotion_holdout_integration.py. Only src import of the module is `from tournament.holdout import HoldoutResult` (promotion.py:46, type-only). core.py:655 literally reads `advisory = decide(grade=prior or "dev_best", gate_results=synth_gates)` — passes NEITHER holdout_result NOR kill_rate; decide()'s signature (promotion.py:128-134) has both as keyword-only optionals defaulting None. core.py:663-672 then drives the persisted rung off `prior` via explicit if-chain, and the docstring at core.py:632-635 confirms 'we don't *consume* its verdict to drive the rung.' Pytest-binding confirmed: holdout.py:97 `if not path.endswith('.py'): continue`; holdout.py:99-102 name must start `test_` or end `_test.py`; holdout.py:170-171 `base = resolve_tool(cwd,'pytest'); args=[*base,'-q','--no-header',...]`; holdout.py:107-108 parser regex `^(?:FAILED|ERROR)\s+`. So a Go `foo_test.go` is filtered out at :97 (not even the name rule).
findings.repro_or_probe: grep -rn 'run_holdout_tests\|extract_baseline_tests' src/ → expect only holdout.py self-refs + the HoldoutResult type import in promotion.py; assert no caller awaits run_holdout_tests. Then a test driving a tournament to promotion_eligible and asserting run_holdout_tests was awaited will FAIL. Python-binding probe: extract_baseline_tests on a repo whose baseline tests are `foo_test.go` returns set() (filtered at holdout.py:97).

findings.title: resolve_tool() — the 'target repo's own tooling' resolver used by test/lint/holdout — is entirely Python-manifest-driven; non-Python repos always fall through to the bare tool name
findings.claim: Confirmed. resolve_tool is presented generically but only understands Python environments (.venv / uv.lock+uv / poetry.lock+poetry / bare tool). Its only callers are the three Python gates (holdout, test_runner, lint); build_check and syntax_check don't even use it. Every non-Python language re-hard-codes its invocation (npx eslint, cargo, go, golangci-lint) rather than going through a shared resolver, so pnpm/yarn workspaces, project-local node_modules/.bin, and a ./gradlew wrapper are never honored. Degrades to PATH (no silent-wrong-pass today) but blocks first-class target-tooling resolution for other languages.
findings.evidence: env.py:68-76 cascade is exactly: `.venv/bin/<tool>` → `uv.lock`+uv (`uv run [--group dev] tool`) → `poetry.lock`+poetry → bare `[tool]`. No node_modules/.bin, no cargo/go/mvn/gradlew branch. grep 'resolve_tool' over src/ → callers are ONLY holdout.py:170, test_runner.py:103, lint.py:94 (all the Python gates; build_check.py and syntax_check.py do NOT call it). Non-Python gates hard-code invocation: lint.py:115 `['npx','eslint','.']`, lint.py:119/123 `cargo clippy`/`golangci-lint run`; test_runner.py:122/126/130 `npm test`/`cargo test`/`go test ./...`. _has_dev_group (env.py:33-39) reads pyproject [dependency-groups]; detect_python_linter (env.py:79-104) is ruff/flake8 + pyproject [tool] only.
findings.repro_or_probe: Unit test: resolve_tool(Path(go_repo),'go') == ['go'] regardless of any toolchain file; resolve_tool(node_repo_with_node_modules,'eslint') ignores node_modules/.bin/eslint. Assert no ecosystem beyond .venv/uv/poetry is recognized.

findings.title: py-only test scoping: hard-coded `tests/unit` default suite and pytest `test_`/`_test.py` naming as the cross-cutting 'is this a test' predicate
findings.claim: Confirmed with one precision fix to the probe wording. Only Python gets diff-scoped test selection; nodejs/rust/go ignore `paths` entirely and run the full suite (npm test / cargo test / go test ./...). The Python path bakes in (a) a hard-coded `tests/unit` default-suite literal for source-only changes and (b) a pytest-specific `test_`/`_test.py`-or-under-`tests/` test-file predicate. CORRECTION to the finder's repro: when a Python repo puts unit tests outside `tests/unit` and a source-only change occurs, `targets=[]` so args become bare `pytest -q`, which COLLECTS EVERYTHING (pytest default discovery), not 'NOTHING' — the over-broad run is the real consequence, not zero coverage. The capability asymmetry (Python scoped, others full-suite-only) is real.
findings.evidence: test_runner.py:46-57: only lang=='python' routes to _run_pytest(paths=paths); nodejs/rust/go map to _run_npm_test/_run_cargo_test/_run_go_test which take only (cwd, timeout_s) — `paths` is never threaded (lines 121-130), so they always run the full suite. _is_test_path (test_runner.py:60-64): `if p.suffix=='.py' and (name startswith test_ or endswith _test.py): return True; return 'tests' in p.parts`. Source-only fallback test_runner.py:111-113: `elif any(p.suffix=='.py' for p in paths): targets = ['tests/unit'] if (cwd/'tests'/'unit').is_dir() else []`. Confirmed the `tests/unit` literal and the pytest naming predicate.
findings.repro_or_probe: Unit test: run_tests(lang='go', paths=[pkg/foo.go]) runs `go test ./...` (paths ignored). Python source-only change with `tests/unit` present scopes to tests/unit; with unit tests in `test/` instead, targets=[] → bare `pytest -q` collects the whole repo (broad, not empty).

findings.title: build_check compiles the TARGET repo with AutoDev's OWN interpreter (sys.executable) and does not use the target's venv — Python build gate can pass/fail for the wrong reason
findings.claim: Confirmed. _run_python_build (and _python_syntax_check) compile the target repo with `sys.executable` (AutoDev's interpreter), not the target's resolved venv/interpreter — unlike the test/lint gates which call resolve_tool. py_compile is pure-syntax/bytecode: it neither sees the target's installed dependencies nor validates against the target's Python version. A repo using newer syntax than AutoDev's interpreter would falsely fail; a 'green' Python build never exercises the target's real dependency-import surface. The other languages get a truer build signal via their real toolchains (cargo check, go build, tsc/npm run build).
findings.evidence: build_check.py:13 `import sys`; build_check.py:86-100 `_run_python_build` runs `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(sys.executable,'-m','py_compile',*py_files,cwd=cwd,...)`. No resolve_tool/.venv anywhere in build_check.py (grep: '.venv' appears only at the exclusion filter line 84). Contrast _run_cargo_check (133-134 `cargo check`) and _run_go_build (137-138 `go build ./...`) which shell out to the real native toolchain, and _run_nodejs_build (114-130 npm run build / tsc). Same sys.executable pattern verified in syntax_check.py:86 (`_python_syntax_check` → sys.executable -m py_compile).
findings.repro_or_probe: Run AutoDev on 3.11 against a repo using 3.12+ syntax: sys.executable py_compile fails though the repo builds under its own 3.12 .venv. Probe: assert build_check resolves the target interpreter (it uses sys.executable today).

findings.title: Symbol index has dedicated extractors only for Python/C++/TS-JS; Go, Rust, Java, Ruby, etc. silently degrade to a regex catch-all (coarser CANDIDATE_FILES digest for the architect)
findings.claim: Confirmed. Exactly three AST-grade extractors are registered: Cpp, Py (real `ast` module), Ts (.ts/.tsx/.js family). Go (.go), Rust (.rs), Java (.java) — and Ruby etc. — have no dedicated extractor and route to the RegexExtractor catch-all (lang_tag 'other'). The regex fallback does include Go/Rust func patterns and a generic class/struct/trait/enum/interface pattern but is self-described as conservative/false-positive-tolerant and misses methods, nested decls, generics nuance, and Java-specific constructs (annotations, records). This feeds the architect a materially noisier CANDIDATE_FILES digest for Go/Rust/Java than for Python — degrades, doesn't break.
findings.evidence: __init__.py:87 `EXTRACTORS.extend([CppExtractor(), PyExtractor(), TsExtractor()])`. Extension sets: py_extractor.py:31 `{'.py'}`; cpp_extractor.py:232-234 `{.cpp,.cc,.cxx,.c,.h,.hpp,.hxx}`; ts_extractor.py:239-241 `{.ts,.tsx,.js,.jsx,.mjs,.cjs}`. grep over the package for `.go`/`.rs`/`.java` in extension/frozenset lines → none. __init__.py:111-114 lookup_extractor falls back to `_regex_extractor()` (RegexExtractor, lang_tag 'other') for any unclaimed suffix. py_extractor.py:12,41 uses the real `ast` module (`import ast`; `tree = ast.parse(source)`). regex_extractor.py:22-34 carries _RE_DEF/_RE_FUNC/_RE_FUNC_GO/_RE_FUNC_RUST + a generic class/struct/trait/enum/interface _RE_CLASS; module docstring (line 9) 'Conservative: lots of false-positives are fine.' RegexExtractor only emits function/class kinds (no method/var/generics handling).
findings.repro_or_probe: lookup_extractor('.go')/('.rs')/('.java') all return RegexExtractor (lang_tag 'other'); ('.py') returns PyExtractor. Feed a Go method `func (r *Repo) Save(...)` + generic `func Map[T any](...)` and compare extracted symbols against tree-sitter to quantify the miss.

findings.title: detect_language ranks Python FIRST and on the weakest possible signal (presence of pyproject.toml/setup.py), so polyglot repos with any Python tooling are misclassified as 'python'
findings.claim: Confirmed. detect_language returns 'python' on the very first check — mere existence of pyproject.toml OR setup.py — before nodejs/rust/go/java/etc. are considered, and it returns a single language for the whole repo. Because every QA gate (build/lint/test/syntax) dispatches on that one string, a JS- or Rust-primary repo that merely carries a pyproject.toml (now common: [tool.ruff], scikit-build/cmake config, dev tooling) gets the Python pytest/ruff/py_compile pipeline and its real toolchain is never run. There is no per-file language map / primary-language scoring. Correct in a Python-primary repo; the root generalization anchor for language routing.
findings.evidence: detect.py:30-31 is the FIRST check: `if (cwd/'pyproject.toml').exists() or (cwd/'setup.py').exists(): return 'python'`, ahead of detect.py:32 `if (cwd/'package.json').exists(): return 'nodejs'` and Cargo.toml/go.mod/pom.xml/build.gradle below it. Function returns ONE string. Dispatch sites confirmed: build_check.py:34, lint.py:38, test_runner.py:42, syntax_check.py:34 all do `lang = language or detect_language(cwd)` and branch on that single string. No per-changed-file language routing exists in the QA gates.
findings.repro_or_probe: Create a dir with a real package.json app + a pyproject.toml containing only [tool.ruff]: detect_language returns 'python', so run_tests runs pytest not `npm test`. Assert this, then design the per-file-language-map / primary-language-scoring fix the other WS-2 agents need.

findings.title: holdout.py only discovers Python tests → VACUOUS pass for JS/TS, AND the holdout runner is dead code (never wired into the live tournament)
findings.claim: CONFIRMED on both legs. (a) holdout.py hard-filters to .py at :97-103 so any JS/TS repo yields an empty baseline → run_holdout_tests vacuously passes at :149-155 (empirically reproduced). (b) The holdout runner is dead in production: extract_baseline_tests/run_holdout_tests have zero src callers; the live ladder (core._next_grade_for_non_a_win) drives the rung off the prior on-disk grade and calls decide() WITHOUT a holdout_result, so promotion.py's holdout-fail branch (:196) is unreachable. JS/TS gets no holdout regression check whether or not the .py filter were fixed.
findings.evidence: Read holdout.py:97-103 `if not path.endswith('.py'): continue` then test_/_test.py filter; _DEFAULT_TEST_DIR='tests' at :34; vacuous-pass at :149-155 `if not baseline_test_paths: return HoldoutResult(passed=True, test_count=0, failure_summary='no baseline tests')`. EMPIRICAL: git repo with tests/foo.test.js + tests/bar.spec.ts → extract_baseline_tests() returned [] → run_holdout_tests() returned passed=True test_count=0 'no baseline tests'. With a mixed .py+.js repo, extract returned only ['tests/test_real.py'] (JS dropped). DEADNESS: `grep -rn extract_baseline_tests|run_holdout_tests src/` → ONLY holdout.py defines/exports them; zero src callers. Only `HoldoutResult` (the dataclass) is imported, by promotion.py:46 for typing. core.py:655 `advisory = decide(grade=prior or 'dev_best', gate_results=synth_gates)` passes NO holdout_result; promotion.py:133 defaults `holdout_result=None`; promotion.py:196 `if holdout_result is not None and not holdout_result.passed:` is therefore unreachable from the only live call site. core.py:632-640 comment: decide 'invoked for telemetry/log instrumentation ... we don't *consume* its verdict to drive the rung'; the ladder is driven off `prior` at :663-672.
findings.repro_or_probe: grep -rn 'extract_baseline_tests\|run_holdout_tests' src/ → only holdout.py. Build a git repo with tests/*.test.js, run extract_baseline_tests(cwd, HEAD) → set(); run_holdout_tests(cwd, that_set) → HoldoutResult(passed=True, test_count=0). To prove deadness: add `raise RuntimeError` inside run_holdout_tests and run the full tournament — it never fires (no src caller).

findings.title: nodejs syntax_check is *.js-ONLY → pure-TypeScript repo gets a vacuous 'no .js files found' pass
findings.claim: CONFIRMED exactly as stated. _nodejs_syntax_check globs only *.js; a pure-TS repo (zero .js) returns passed=True 'no .js files found' — a silent wrong-pass on syntactically broken .ts/.tsx (empirically reproduced). .jsx/.mjs/.cjs are also silently ignored. The only TS syntax/type coverage left is build_check's tsc path, which is itself broken (see next finding).
findings.evidence: Read syntax_check.py:117-121 `js_files = [str(p) for p in cwd.rglob('*.js') if 'node_modules' not in p.parts and '.venv' not in p.parts]`; :122-123 `if not js_files: return GateResult(passed=True, details='no .js files found')`; docstring :114-115 'TypeScript files are intentionally excluded because Node cannot parse TS syntax directly.' EMPIRICAL: /tmp repo with package.json + a.ts (unclosed `export function f(){`) + b.tsx (`const x: number = ;`) → run_syntax_check(cwd,'nodejs') returned passed=True, details='no .js files found'. Also confirmed .jsx/.mjs/.cjs are not globbed (only *.js).
findings.repro_or_probe: mkdir /tmp/ts; echo '{"name":"t"}' > /tmp/ts/package.json; printf 'export function f(){\n' > /tmp/ts/a.ts; PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "import asyncio;from pathlib import Path;from qa.syntax_check import run_syntax_check;print(asyncio.run(run_syntax_check(Path('/tmp/ts'),'nodejs')))" → passed=True 'no .js files found'.

findings.title: build_check `npx tsc --noEmit` is a FALSE-NEGATIVE BLOCK for any TS repo without tsconfig.json (and resolves to a wrong `tsc` when typescript not local)
findings.claim: CONFIRMED. The npx-tsc fallback hard-blocks (passed=False) on any TS repo lacking a build script + tsconfig: a tooling/config mismatch is reported to the recovery layer as 'tsc build check failed' + help/banner text, as if the diff broke the build. I additionally reproduced the worse variant: with no local typescript, `npx tsc` resolves to an unrelated system tsc (Tcl/Tk) and still blocks. tsc is also never handed the changed files, so even when it runs, coverage depends entirely on the project tsconfig include.
findings.evidence: Read build_check.py:114-130: _run_nodejs_build runs `npm run build` only if a 'build' script exists (:124-127), else falls back to `['npx','tsc','--noEmit']` (:128-129) with no -p/tsconfig and no file args. _run_subprocess returns passed=False with the captured output when returncode!=0 (:74-76). EMPIRICAL: /tmp repo with package.json (no build script, no tsconfig) + a.ts → run_build_check(cwd,'nodejs') returned passed=False, details begins 'tsc build check failed:' followed by the Tcl/Tk banner 'This is not the tsc command you are looking for' — because tsc is not on PATH here and `npx tsc` resolved to the system Tcl tsc, exactly the spurious-block failure mode the finder described. (With a real local typescript, npx tsc with no project prints the tsc help screen and exits 1 → same passed=False block.)
findings.repro_or_probe: mkdir /tmp/tsb; echo '{"name":"t"}' > /tmp/tsb/package.json; printf 'export const x=1;\n' > /tmp/tsb/a.ts; PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "import asyncio;from pathlib import Path;from qa.build_check import run_build_check;print(asyncio.run(run_build_check(Path('/tmp/tsb'),'nodejs')))" → passed=False, details 'tsc build check failed:\n<help/banner>'.

findings.title: nodejs test gate runs unscoped `npm test` and BLOCKS when there is no `test` script — no diff-scoping, no 'no tests' soft path like Python
findings.claim: CONFIRMED. _run_npm_test is bare `npm test` with no use of the `paths` diff-scope (empirically: a source-only path still ran the full suite) and no 'no test script' soft-pass: a package.json lacking a `test` script makes `npm test` exit 1 → passed=False → BLOCK on every task, even for a correct change (empirically reproduced). This is a loud false-negative (blocks rather than silently wrong-passes), and the unscoped full-suite run is a scale concern on monorepos.
findings.evidence: Read test_runner.py:121-122 `async def _run_npm_test(cwd, *, timeout_s): return await _run_subprocess(['npm','test'], ...)` — bare, no paths. run_tests forwards `paths` ONLY to the python branch (:47); the nodejs runner is dispatched at :49-57 with no paths. Python branch has the soft 'no python changes' pass (:115) and bounded targets (:108-113); nodejs has none. EMPIRICAL #1: /tmp repo package.json `"scripts":{}` → run_tests() returned passed=False, details 'npm test tests failed:\nnpm error Missing script: "test"'. EMPIRICAL #2: /tmp repo with a passing `test` script, called run_tests(cwd, paths=[Path('foo.js')]) (source-only change) → passed=True 'npm test tests passed' i.e. it ran the WHOLE suite, ignoring paths.
findings.repro_or_probe: mkdir /tmp/nt; echo '{"name":"t","scripts":{}}' > /tmp/nt/package.json; PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "import asyncio;from pathlib import Path;from qa.test_runner import run_tests;print(asyncio.run(run_tests(Path('/tmp/nt'))))" → passed=False 'Missing script: test'. Fix: detect missing `test` script and soft-pass; honor `paths` for JS too.

findings.title: No package-manager resolution for JS — env.py handles only .venv/uv/poetry; all JS gates hardcode npm/npx, ignoring yarn/pnpm/corepack
findings.claim: CONFIRMED. resolve_tool (env.py:56-76) is Python-only with zero Node awareness, and the JS gates don't call it anyway — they hardcode npm/npx. There is no Node tool resolution at all: yarn-only / pnpm-only repos get npm invocations that may run against a wrong/desynced lockfile or fail to resolve workspace scripts. yarn.lock/pnpm-lock.yaml exist in src solely as diff-review skip globs. Not a silent-wrong-pass, so 'should'.
findings.evidence: Read env.py:68-76: resolve_tool cascade is .venv/bin → uv.lock+uv → poetry.lock+poetry → bare [tool]; no node/yarn/pnpm branch. JS gates never call resolve_tool: test_runner.py:122 `['npm','test']`; lint.py:115 `['npx','eslint','.']`; build_check.py:126 `['npm','run','build']` / :129 `['npx','tsc','--noEmit']`. `grep -rn 'yarn\|pnpm\|corepack\|packageManager' src/` → ONLY execute_phase.py:6802-6803 (yarn.lock/pnpm-lock.yaml inside _REVIEW_GENERATED_FILE_GLOBS, a diff-review skip list at :6799), never for tool selection. No corepack/packageManager handling anywhere.
findings.repro_or_probe: Create a pnpm workspace (pnpm-lock.yaml, package.json with packageManager:'pnpm@9', a script resolving only under pnpm). run_tests/run_build_check invoke npm → wrong resolution. Fix: add resolve_node_runner(cwd) keyed off pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock / packageManager.

findings.title: Mixed Python+JS/TS repo routes ALL gates to Python — a TS bug fix in a repo that also has pyproject.toml gets zero JS-aware verification
findings.claim: CONFIRMED. detect_language gives pyproject.toml/setup.py precedence over package.json and returns one repo-global value, computed once at execute_phase.py:7515 and reused for all gates. In a polyglot repo (Python + TS) a .ts-only diff is verified entirely by Python tooling (ruff/py_compile/pytest) — eslint/tsc/npm test never run. Green gates on an unverified TS change = silent wrong-pass. Language is never routed per changed file.
findings.evidence: Read detect.py:30-33: `if (cwd/'pyproject.toml').exists() or (cwd/'setup.py').exists(): return 'python'` BEFORE `if (cwd/'package.json').exists(): return 'nodejs'`. execute_phase.py:7515 `language = detect_language(cwd)` computed once; threaded as the single `language` into syntax (:7575), lint (:7576), build (:7577) and (implicitly via detect inside run_tests) test (:7578). EMPIRICAL: /tmp repo with pyproject.toml + package.json(test:vitest) → detect_language() returned 'python'. Confirmed each gate routes on that single value: syntax_check.py:38, lint.py:42, build_check.py:34-44, test_runner.py:46 all branch on `lang=='python'` first. No per-changed-file language routing exists.
findings.repro_or_probe: mkdir /tmp/mix; printf '[project]\nname="x"\n' > /tmp/mix/pyproject.toml; echo '{"name":"f","scripts":{"test":"vitest run"}}' > /tmp/mix/package.json; PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from pathlib import Path;from qa.detect import detect_language;print(detect_language(Path('/tmp/mix')))" → 'python'. Fix: route gates by the language of the changed files (paths), not the root manifest.

findings.title: TS/JS symbol extraction is genuinely first-class (tree-sitter present, high fidelity); regex fallback under-extracts non-exported arrow consts but is acceptable
findings.claim: Substance CONFIRMED, one citation off. TsExtractor is registered (__init__.py line 87, the finder wrote :90/:84-91 — the extend call is at 87) for all six JS/TS extensions; TS_TREESITTER_AVAILABLE=True here so the tree-sitter path runs and captures non-exported arrow consts (empirically [('h','var'),('a','var')]). The regex fallback's _RE_EXPORT_CONST requires the `export` keyword, so a bare `const helper = () =>` is dropped only when the native binding is absent — an explicitly scoped best-effort tradeoff. Marked 'partial' solely for the line-number drift; the working-leg conclusion stands.
findings.evidence: Read ts_extractor.py:239-241: extensions = {.ts,.tsx,.js,.jsx,.mjs,.cjs}; :244-250 extract() prefers _extract_via_treesitter then falls back to _extract_via_regex; :253 exports TS_TREESITTER_AVAILABLE. __init__.py:87 (NOT :90 as the finder cited) `EXTRACTORS.extend([CppExtractor(), PyExtractor(), TsExtractor()])`. EMPIRICAL: TS_TREESITTER_AVAILABLE=True; TsExtractor().extract('const h=()=>1;\nexport const a=()=>2;') returned [('h','var'),('a','var')] — the non-exported `const h` arrow fn IS captured via tree-sitter, refuting any fidelity worry for the native path.
findings.repro_or_probe: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from state.language_extractors.ts_extractor import TsExtractor,TS_TREESITTER_AVAILABLE;print(TS_TREESITTER_AVAILABLE);print([(s['name'],s['kind']) for s in TsExtractor().extract('const h=()=>1;\nexport const a=()=>2;')])" → True / [('h','var'),('a','var')]. To exercise the fallback gap, force TS_TREESITTER_AVAILABLE=False and confirm `h` is dropped.

findings.title: Holdout gate is pytest-only AND unwired in production: Go (and every non-Python repo) gets a vacuous holdout pass
findings.claim: The promotion-grade holdout gate is hard pytest-only (extract_baseline_tests filters to .py test_/_test.py files; run_holdout_tests always invokes pytest) so for a Go repo it returns a vacuous HoldoutResult(passed=True, test_count=0). MORE DECISIVELY, the gate is entirely dead for ALL languages: extract_baseline_tests/run_holdout_tests have no production caller, and holdout_result is never once passed into promotion.decide() (the sole decide() call at core.py:655 omits it and is telemetry-only per its own docstring), so promotion.py:196 (the holdout block rule) can never fire. The Go vacuous-pass is moot — nothing gates at the holdout altitude for any language.
findings.evidence: Read holdout.py: line 97 `if not path.endswith('.py'): continue`; line 99-102 requires `test_`/`_test.py` name; line 149-155 `if not baseline_test_paths: return HoldoutResult(passed=True, test_count=0,...)`; line 170 `base = resolve_tool(cwd, 'pytest')` always. Wiring: `git grep -ln 'extract_baseline_tests|run_holdout_tests' -- '*.py'` returns ONLY src/tournament/holdout.py (self), tests/test_promotion_holdout_integration.py, tests/test_tournament_holdout.py — zero production callers. `git grep -n 'holdout_result=' -- 'src/*.py'` returns NOTHING — holdout_result is never passed to decide(). promotion.py:133 defaults `holdout_result=None`; promotion.py:196 `if holdout_result is not None and not holdout_result.passed` can never fire. core.py:655 is the ONLY decide() call site: `advisory = decide(grade=prior or 'dev_best', gate_results=synth_gates)` (no holdout_result), and core.py:632-640 docstring says decide is invoked for telemetry only and its verdict is NOT consumed to drive the rung.
findings.repro_or_probe: `git grep -ln 'extract_baseline_tests' -- '*.py'` → only holdout.py + 2 test files. `git grep -n 'holdout_result=' -- 'src/*.py'` → empty. `grep -n 'decide(' src/tournament/core.py` → single call at :655 with no holdout_result. findings.title: `go test ./...` on a Go repo with NO test files exits 0 → test_runner gate silently vacuously passes a Go bug-fix
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly as stated. `go test ./...` on a Go package with no *_test.go files exits 0 → test_runner returns passed=True ('go tests passed') having executed zero assertions. The `paths` (changed-files) arg is dropped for Go at test_runner.py:57 (only Python's _run_pytest receives it), so there is no diff-scoped 'no test covers this change' reasoning and no non-vacuous guard. A Go bug-fix in a no-test package clears the blocking test_runner gate (cfg.test_runner defaults True) with nothing verified.
findings.evidence: Read test_runner.py: line 91-92 `if proc.returncode == 0: return GateResult(passed=True, details=f'{tool_name} tests passed')`. Line 49-57 dispatch builds `runners = {... 'go': _run_go_test}` and `return await runner(cwd, timeout_s=timeout_s)` — `paths` is NOT forwarded. Line 129-130 `_run_go_test(cwd, *, timeout_s)` has no `paths` param and runs `['go','test','./...']`. Empirical (real go 1.x via homebrew): created module m with one non-test f.go, `go test ./...` printed `?  m  [no test files]` and `exit=0` → passes through line 91-92 as passed=True. Note the Python branch (line 105-115) DOES consult `paths` and has a 'no python changes' short-circuit; the Go branch has none.

mkdir m; printf 'module m
go 1.21
'>m/go.mod; printf 'package m
func F() int{return 1}
'>m/f.go; (cd m && go test ./...; echo $?) → '[no test files]' exit 0 (verified). Fix: thread `paths` into _run_go_test and treat test_count==0 as a loud degrade (warn/no-test signal) rather than a clean block-severity pass.

findings.title: Go build/test/lint gates convert 'toolchain absent' into a silent PASS (FileNotFoundError → passed=True)
findings.claim: Confirmed and empirically reproduced. When `go`/`golangci-lint` are absent from PATH, build_check + test_runner + lint each return passed=True via the FileNotFoundError branch (graceful degradation, block-severity clean pass, no loud signal). is_repo_unbuildable()/RUNNABLE_TEST_LANGUAGES key off go.mod presence only and do NOT verify the toolchain is installed (no shutil.which), so a Go repo with no `go` binary green-washes through three gates and is never routed to the unrunnable-tests soft-pass path.
findings.evidence: Read all three: build_check.py:68-69 `except FileNotFoundError: return GateResult(passed=True, details=f'{tool_name} not found, skipping build check')`; test_runner.py:85-86 same pattern ('skipping tests'); lint.py:75-76 same ('skipping lint'). detect.py:99-108 RUNNABLE_TEST_LANGUAGES includes 'go' with no PATH check; detect.py:111-118 is_repo_unbuildable returns `lang is None or lang not in RUNNABLE_TEST_LANGUAGES` — no shutil.which. `grep shutil src/qa/detect.py` → none. EMPIRICAL (project .venv python, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin so `go` absent): run_build_check(go_repo,'go') → passed=True, details='go build not found, skipping build check'; is_repo_unbuildable(go_repo) → False. So with no go binary all three blocking gates pass having executed nothing, and the repo is still declared buildable.
findings.repro_or_probe: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin .venv/bin/python -c "import asyncio,pathlib,shutil; from qa.build_check import run_build_check; print(shutil.which('go')); print(asyncio.run(run_build_check(pathlib.Path('/path/to/go/repo'),'go')))" → None, GateResult(passed=True,'go build not found, skipping build check') [verified]. Fix: when detect_language=='go' and shutil.which('go') is None, degrade with a visible severity or route through is_repo_unbuildable (add a PATH check there), not a clean block-severity pass.

findings.title: Go symbol extraction falls to RegexExtractor which MISSES every Go type (struct/interface) declaration
findings.claim: Confirmed. There is no Go LanguageExtractor (EXTRACTORS holds Cpp/Py/Ts only), so .go files route to RegexExtractor. _RE_FUNC_GO catches `func Name(`/`func (recv) Name(`, but _RE_CLASS requires the keyword immediately before the name (`struct Server`) whereas Go writes `type Server struct {`/`type Reader interface {` — so every Go struct and interface (Go's primary abstraction unit) is missed by the FTS symbol index that feeds the architect's CANDIDATE_FILES digest. Empirically verified: only the two funcs extracted, both type decls absent.
findings.evidence: Read __init__.py:83-87 `EXTRACTORS.extend([CppExtractor(), PyExtractor(), TsExtractor()])` — no Go extractor; lookup_extractor (line 110-114) returns RegexExtractor (lang_tag 'other') for unmatched .go suffix. regex_extractor.py:27 `_RE_FUNC_GO = re.compile(r'^\s*func\s+(?:\([^)]*\)\s+)?([A-Za-z_]\w{0,63})\s*\(')` catches funcs/methods; line 31-34 `_RE_CLASS` matches `(class|struct|trait|enum|interface) Name` i.e. keyword-then-name. Go is `type Name struct {` (type-then-name). EMPIRICAL: extract on Go sample returned only `function Start line 7` and `function NewServer line 8`; `_RE_CLASS.match('type Server struct {')` → None, `_RE_CLASS.match('type Reader interface {')` → None. Both struct and interface invisible.
findings.repro_or_probe: .venv/bin/python -c "from state.language_extractors.regex_extractor import RegexExtractor as R; print(R().extract('type Server struct {\n}\nfunc (s *Server) Start() error { return nil }'))" → only the func [verified]. Fix: add a Go extractor (tree-sitter-go preferred, regex fallback `^\s*type\s+(\w+)\s+(struct|interface)\b`) and register it in EXTRACTORS at __init__.py:87.

findings.title: Go build_check is whole-tree `go build ./...` ignoring the 60s default timeout headroom and the diff scope — fine functionally but unbounded at scale
findings.claim: Confirmed. _run_go_build runs whole-tree `go build ./...` (no diff scoping) under build_check's hardcoded 60s default (_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=60), and execute_phase.py:7577 passes no override — unlike test_runner (cfg.test_timeout_s) and lint (cfg.lint_timeout_s), which the orchestrator DOES override. Strengthening: there is no build_check_timeout_s config field at all, so the 60s ceiling cannot be raised. On a large/cold Go module `go build ./...` exceeds 60s → TimeoutError branch returns passed=False (hard block). Thus Go build_check flips from vacuous-green (small/absent toolchain) to spurious-red (large), surfacing loudly rather than as a silent wrong-pass.
findings.evidence: Read build_check.py:20 `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 60`; line 137-138 `_run_go_build` → `_run_subprocess(['go','build','./...'], cwd, timeout_s=timeout_s)` (whole module, no diff scope); line 71 `except asyncio.TimeoutError: return GateResult(passed=False, details=f'{tool_name} build check timed out')` (hard block). execute_phase.py:7577 `('build_check', cfg.build_check, lambda: run_build_check(cwd, language))` — NO timeout override, so the 60s default applies, in contrast to line 7578 `run_tests(..., timeout_s=cfg.test_timeout_s)` and line 7576 `run_lint(..., timeout_s=cfg.lint_timeout_s)`. Confirmed via grep of config/schema.py: only `test_timeout_s=600.0` (line 763) and `lint_timeout_s=120.0` (line 768) exist — there is NO build_check_timeout_s knob, so build_check is structurally pinned to 60s with no override path.
findings.repro_or_probe: grep -n 'timeout_s' src/orchestrator/execute_phase.py around 7576-7578 shows build_check alone lacks a timeout arg; grep -n 'build_check_timeout_s' src/config/schema.py → no match (only test_timeout_s/lint_timeout_s exist) [verified]. Fix: add cfg.build_check_timeout_s (mirroring test_timeout_s) and thread it at execute_phase.py:7577, and/or scope `go build` to changed packages.

findings.title: The NON-VACUOUS holdout gate is Python/pytest-ONLY by construction — for non-Python languages it extracts zero baseline tests and passes vacuously
findings.claim: The holdout module is Python/pytest-only by construction (holdout.py:97-98 .py filter, :170 resolve_tool 'pytest', :149-155 empty->vacuous pass) — VERIFIED for non-Python (Go test excluded; empty set vacuous pass). So holdout is currently dead code that runs for no language. The 'Python-only vacuity' is real at the code level but its promotion-gate impact is masked by total non-invocation; the true defect is two-layered (Python-only AND unwired), and the north-star 'non-vacuous holdout' is unmet for an even more basic reason than language coverage.

HOWEVER, the IMPACT framing is REFUTED: `grep -rn 'run_holdout_tests|extract_baseline_tests' src/` returns ZERO call sites outside holdout.py. promotion.decide() has exactly one production call site (core.py:655) which passes synth_gates=[GateResult(passed=True,'judges-confirmed')] and does NOT pass holdout_result (defaults None). promotion.py:46 imports HoldoutResult only for a type annotation. So the holdout gate is DEAD/UNWIRED in production — it never runs for ANY language, Python included. The finder's claim that 'the whole tournament promotion ladder relies on' it and that 'a non-Python winner reaches promotion_eligible with zero holdout verification' is moot: no winner of any language is holdout-verified at runtime.
