findings.title: Seed CONFIRMED + quantified: only Py/TS/C++ have real extractors; Go/Rust/Java/Ruby fall to RegexExtractor, which misses ~60-67% of meaningful symbols in a representative probe
findings.claim: Only CppExtractor/PyExtractor/TsExtractor are registered (__init__.py:87); every other suffix falls to RegexExtractor (lang_tag='other', __init__.py:114). On representative files the regex fallback returned 3/8 Go and 3/9 Java meaningful symbols, missing the same symbols the finder listed. Missing symbols cannot produce symbol_hits or the +0.5 file boost (file_index.py:1520-1523), degrading the architect's candidate_files digest for exactly the Go/Rust/Java languages v1.0 promises first-class. One caveat: caught symbols still index their full source line as `signature` (FTS-indexed), so a spec token can sometimes hit a caught symbol's signature even if not its name — but a MISSED symbol contributes nothing.
findings.evidence: __init__.py:87 `EXTRACTORS.extend([CppExtractor(), PyExtractor(), TsExtractor()])`; __init__.py:110-114 lookup loops EXTRACTORS then `return _regex_extractor()`. My probe (PYTHONPATH=src lookup_extractor('.go').extract) on an 8-symbol Go file returned exactly 3 (function NewProcessor, function Charge, function refund); MISSED Processor, Logger, Map, DefaultRate, ErrInsufficient = 3/8. Java 9-symbol file returned exactly 3 (class InvoiceService, class Status, class Repository); MISSED createInvoice, computeTotal, max, save, LineItem, MAX_ITEMS = 3/9. Both match the finding's numbers. Downstream chain independently confirmed: file_index.py:632 extractor.extract; symbols_fts schema (file_index.py:258-259) indexes name/file_path/signature; get_candidates_for_spec at 1511-1526 scores symbol hits (+1.0) and boosts implicated file (+0.5 at line 1523); framing_signals.py:74 reads symbol_hits[].file_path; plan_phase.py:769 calls get_candidates_for_spec and injects at 818 as candidate_files.
findings.repro_or_probe: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from state.language_extractors import lookup_extractor; print([(s['kind'],s['name']) for s in lookup_extractor('.go').extract(open('x.go').read())])" → 3 symbols; compare to go/ast (8). Confirmed reproducible.

findings.title: Java methods are 100% invisible: RegexExtractor has NO pattern for `modifier returnType name(...)`
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly as stated. RegexExtractor extracts zero Java/C#/Kotlin/Scala methods because no pattern matches the `modifier returnType name(...)` shape; all four representative method lines return NO MATCH from every pattern. Since the method name is absent from both the symbol `name` and the (class-head) `signature`, _tokenize_spec tokens for a method can only hit class-level names — the digest cannot point the architect at the right method/file for Java repos. Silent quality hole, not a crash.
findings.evidence: regex_extractor.py:22-34 shows the only function patterns are _RE_DEF (def), _RE_FUNC (function), _RE_FUNC_GO (func), _RE_FUNC_RUST (fn) — none match `<modifier> <ret-type> <name>(`. I matched all four Java method lines against all five patterns individually: 'public Invoice createInvoice(...)' -> NO MATCH; 'private double computeTotal(...)' -> NO MATCH; 'static int max(...)' -> NO MATCH; 'void save(...)' -> NO MATCH. Full-file probe returned only class/enum/interface heads (InvoiceService, Status, Repository), zero methods. Because methods aren't extracted, their names never enter symbols_fts (the class-head signature line doesn't contain them), so a spec token like 'createInvoice' cannot hit any symbol row (FTS schema file_index.py:258-259).
findings.repro_or_probe: Confirmed: assert ('createInvoice','function') in RegexExtractor().extract(java_src) FAILS; per-line regex match test shows NO MATCH for all four method shapes.

findings.title: Go generics blindness: `func Map[K any](...)` never matches because _RE_FUNC_GO requires `name\s*\(`
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly. _RE_FUNC_GO (regex_extractor.py:27) requires `(` immediately after the name (modulo whitespace), so any Go generic `func Name[...](...)` is silently dropped. Rust's _RE_FUNC_RUST already permits `<` via its `[<(]` terminator; Go was not given the same treatment. Trivially fixable by mirroring the Rust terminator.
findings.evidence: regex_extractor.py:27 `_RE_FUNC_GO = re.compile(r"^\s*func\s+(?:\([^)]*\)\s+)?([A-Za-z_]\w{0,63})\s*\(")` — terminator is `\(` so a `[...]` type-param list before the paren breaks it. Probe: `_RE_FUNC_GO.match('func Map[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V) map[K]V {')` returned None; `_RE_FUNC_GO.match('func Map(m int) int {')` returned a match (span 0-9). Generic `Map` was in the MISSED set of the Go full-file probe. Confirmed the contrast claim too: _RE_FUNC_RUST (line 29) ends in `[<(]` so `fn generic<T>(...)` matches (span 0-11), while Go's pattern lacks the same allowance.
findings.repro_or_probe: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from state.language_extractors.regex_extractor import _RE_FUNC_GO; print(_RE_FUNC_GO.match('func Map[K any](m int) int {'))" → None. Confirmed.

findings.title: Rust `pub` modifier blindness: `pub struct/trait/enum` are dropped because _RE_CLASS's modifier alternation lacks `pub`
findings.claim: Confirmed. _RE_CLASS lacks Rust's `pub` (and `pub(crate)` etc.) in its modifier alternation, so all exported `pub struct/trait/enum` decls fail to match while bare forms match — which is why the existing test (bare forms only) passes. Exported items are the spec-relevant ones, so this is a real Rust fidelity loss. One-token regex fix.
findings.evidence: regex_extractor.py:31-33 _RE_CLASS modifier group is `(?:public\s+|private\s+|abstract\s+|final\s+|sealed\s+)?` — no `pub`. Probe: `_RE_CLASS.match('pub struct Engine {')` returned None; `_RE_CLASS.match('struct Engine {')` matched (span 0-13). Full Rust file probe MISSED Engine (pub struct), Charger (pub trait), State (pub enum), LIMIT (pub const). The proposed fix (add `pub(?:\s*\([^)]*\))?\s+`) is sound.
findings.repro_or_probe: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from state.language_extractors.regex_extractor import _RE_CLASS; print(bool(_RE_CLASS.match('pub struct Engine {')))" → False. Confirmed.

findings.title: Go/Rust methods are mislabeled kind='function' and lose their receiver/impl type; the only Go/Rust test avoids every realistic shape, so the degradation ships green
findings.claim: The test-coverage gap is real and is the important half: tests/test_state_language_extractors.py:115-138 is the sole Go/Rust assertion and only checks bare top-level shapes, so a regression worsening Go/Java/Rust extraction would not be caught (no Java case exists at all). The kind-mislabel is real but low-impact and partly overstated: RegexExtractor emits kind='function' for Go receiver/Rust impl methods (vs PyExtractor's 'method'), but the receiver/impl type is preserved in the FTS-indexed `signature` (full source line), so it is searchable — only the structured kind tag is wrong, and kind is not used as a scoring weight (file_index.py:1520, +1.0 per hit). Minor: the finder's specific Rust count (3) undercounts by one (trait-body `fn` is caught -> 4).
findings.evidence: Test (lines 115-138) asserts only DoThing/rust_thing/python_thing/TopClass; docstring at :116 claims it 'handles e.g. Go / Rust / Ruby shapes' but no method/type/generic/pub/Java case is asserted — the green-because-nothing-hard pattern is real. RegexExtractor hardcodes kind='function' for every function regex (regex_extractor.py:54-58), confirmed: Go `func (p *Processor) Charge(...)` yields kind='function' (not 'method'), while PyExtractor labels class methods kind='method' (py_extractor.py:84, probe: method __init__/create_invoice/_compute_total). HOWEVER two sub-claims are weaker than stated: (1) The receiver/impl type is NOT fully 'lost' — the symbol's `signature` is the full source line ('func (p *Processor) Charge(amount float64) float64 {', confirmed via probe), and `signature` IS FTS-indexed (file_index.py:259), so the receiver type `Processor` survives and is searchable; only the structured `kind` tag is wrong. (2) The finder's parenthetical Rust enumeration in finding 4 ('only new/process/helper caught', 3 symbols) is slightly off: my Rust probe caught 4 because the trait body line `fn charge(&self...)` also matched _RE_FUNC_RUST. The kind-not-used-in-scoring claim is essentially correct: kind appears in the score-key tuple (file_index.py:1513-1519) for identity/dedup but is never used as a weight — score is purely +1.0 per hit (line 1520).
findings.repro_or_probe: Add probe tests asserting RegexExtractor on Go `type X struct`/`func (r *X) M()`/`func G[T any]()` and on a Java method return those symbols — all FAIL today. Also assert Go receiver method kind=='method' — FAILS (returns 'function'). Confirmed: Charge symbol has kind='function' but signature contains 'func (p *Processor)'.

findings.title: Resolver's deterministic STRUCTURAL actions (re_architect/re_plan/narrow_scope/split_task) are inert by construction: prose rationale parses to 0 corrective tasks, so they always fall through to the legacy block
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly as stated. For every structural failure class (all conflict_* via re_architect, dag_invalid/cross_phase_dag_invalid via re_plan, edit_scope_violation via narrow_scope->re_plan, and any split_task), the deterministic resolver returns a structural action whose only direction text is a prose rationale with no bullets. parse_corrective_direction yields 0 tasks, so _resolver_corrective returns None and the chokepoint always falls through to the legacy block. The resolver records resolution_chosen (looks engaged) but never recovers — guaranteed inertness for the entire structural rung family.
findings.evidence: execute_phase.py:1763-1765 confirmed verbatim: `if a in ("split_task","narrow_scope","re_architect","re_plan"): direction = str(params.get("direction") or rationale or ""); return await _resolver_corrective(orch, task, direction)`. blocker_resolver.py _act (110-114) builds ResolutionAction(params=dict(params),...) — the structural rungs (e.g. line 250 `_act("re_architect", rationale=...)`) pass NO direction kwarg, so params={} and direction=rationale (prose). I ran the finder's probe: `parse_corrective_direction('merge conflict could not be resolved mechanically: rethink...', phase_id='1', base_task_count=2, max_tasks=8)` -> produced=0; bullet input `- task one\n- task two` -> produced=2. corrective_parser.py:79-80 short-circuits empty; _split_top_level_bullets (131-156) only matches _RE_TOP_LEVEL_BULLET `^[ ]?(?:[-*]|\d+\.)\s+` so prose yields []. _resolver_corrective (1713-1714) `if not corrective_tasks: return None` -> _apply_resolution returns None -> caller does legacy block. Chain fully traced.
findings.repro_or_probe: Confirmed by probe: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from orchestrator.corrective_parser import parse_corrective_direction; print(len(parse_corrective_direction('merge conflict could not be resolved mechanically: rethink the task at component altitude so the patches stop colliding.', phase_id='1', base_task_count=2, max_tasks=8)))"` -> 0. Stronger test: drive block_task with failure_class=CONFLICT_3WAY_FAILED under resolver_enabled and assert out.status != 'blocked' — will FAIL (falls through).

findings.title: The resolver is integration-untested in its shipped (on-by-default) configuration: conftest disables it for all but 4 tests, and 0 of those drive the real execute loop
findings.claim: Confirmed. The autouse conftest fixture forces AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED=1 for every test lacking the resolver_enabled marker. Production ships enabled=True (schema.py:566, defaults.py:313). Only 4 files carry the marker; the 2 that touch the execute loop (engagement, wiring) call block_task / _maybe_resolve_blocker DIRECTLY — none drives run_execute_phase/_run_task/the phase loop with the resolver on. So the resolver's precedence vs the legacy ladder, budget escalation, and firing rate across a realistic task lifecycle have zero end-to-end coverage in the shipped config; CI green-lights the OFF path while production ships the ON path.
findings.evidence: conftest.py:16 `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)` on `_resolver_disabled_by_default`; lines 35-38: `if request.node.get_closest_marker("resolver_enabled"): monkeypatch.delenv("AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED",...) else: monkeypatch.setenv("AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED","1")`. schema.py:566 `_default_resolver_cfg` returns `ResolverConfig(enabled=True,...)`; defaults.py:313 `resolver=ResolverConfig(enabled=True,...)`. `grep -rl resolver_enabled tests/` = 4 files (conftest.py, test_resolver_engagement.py, test_specialist_role_dispatch.py, test_execute_phase_resolver_wiring.py). Wiring test entrypoints all `await ep._maybe_resolve_blocker(...)` (lines 105,118,133,148,166,195,217). Engagement test entrypoints all `await block_task(...)` (124,166,203,206). Quant: files touching run_execute_phase/_run_task/execute_phase = 59; of those resolver_enabled = 2; grep for run_execute_phase|_run_task across all 4 resolver_enabled files returned NO hits.
findings.repro_or_probe: Add an integration test marked resolver_enabled that runs the real per-task execute loop with a stub adapter producing persistent developer failure, and assert a resolution_outcome=recovered ledger op precedes any blocked transition. No such test exists today; writing it would expose findings #1 and #5.

findings.title: Resolver is reachable from the loop ONLY after the full legacy ladder (REFINE/PIVOT/WEB_SEARCH/ARCHITECT_CONSULT) exhausts for developer failures — it is precedence-shadowed, not unwired
findings.claim: Confirmed as a precedence-SHADOWING claim for the dominant developer-failure path: developer failures route to _try_retry_or_escalate (4474), where the legacy escalation_ladder absorbs early cycles as continue (discard 0..2) / REFINE / PIVOT / WEB_SEARCH / ARCHITECT_CONSULT and only reaches block_task (and thus the resolver chokepoint) at the SOFT_BLOCKER rung (5853) or retry-exhaustion tail (6053) — both inside _try_retry_or_escalate. So a stuck developer task may terminate via PIVOT/quarantine before block_task is ever reached, which structurally explains the Run-6 '0 fires / shadowed by recovery_action_chosen' note (the F1d invariant holds; the resolver is simply downstream of a ladder that handles most cases first). CORRECTION to the finder: block_task is NOT reached only at 5853/6053 — guardrail_exceeded (4392/4605) and several other failure classes call block_task directly without the escalation ladder, so those classes DO reach the resolver promptly. The shadowing is specific to the discard/refine/pivot developer-retry path, not universal.
findings.evidence: execute_phase.py:4474 (in _execute_one) `task = await _try_retry_or_escalate(orch, task, retry_limit, reason=...)` for developer failures. escalation_ladder.py:189-194: `if discard_count >= _DISCARD_PIVOT_THRESHOLD: baseline='PIVOT' elif >= _DISCARD_REFINE_THRESHOLD: baseline='REFINE' else: baseline='continue'`; SOFT_BLOCKER/ARCHITECT_CONSULT/WEB_SEARCH gates at 168-188. execute_phase.py:5700 `if step != "continue":` gates escalation dispatch. AST enclosing-func check: 5853 and 6053 (the SOFT_BLOCKER + retry-exhaustion block_task calls) are BOTH inside `_try_retry_or_escalate`; 4474 is inside `_execute_one`. recovery_action_chosen op emitted at ~5680 regardless. HOWEVER: the finder's 'block_task reached ONLY at 5853/6053' is overstated — _execute_one ALSO calls block_task directly at 4392/4605 (guardrail_exceeded, exception-driven, NOT via the ladder), and there are ~14 other block_task sites (1415/1525/1569 in _dispatch_architect_consult; 2141-2203; 2452; 4670/4749/4875; 5216/5254).
findings.repro_or_probe: Field probe: run a deterministically-failing developer task and count blocker_escalated vs recovery_action_chosen + stuck_refine/stuck_pivot ops across the run; the latter dominate. To check the correction, contrast with a guardrail-exceeded task which reaches block_task (and the resolver) on the first exception.

findings.title: Quarantine (typed infra halt) is a fully separate channel that bypasses the resolver — no recovery decision is recorded for it
findings.claim: Confirmed that quarantine bypasses the resolver: AuthenticationFailedError / InfrastructureCircuitOpenError stamp 'quarantined' directly via update_task_status with no resolver breadcrumb (no blocker_escalated/resolution_chosen), and the INFRA_CIRCUIT_OPEN -> fall_through rung in blocker_resolver.py:160 is dead code for the live quarantine path. CORRECTION: the finder calls quarantine a 'terminal-pending sink' and says it 'violates the single-coherent-channel invariant' / overstates F1d — but the code explicitly designs quarantine as NON-TERMINAL and resumable (docstring 2686-2691). The F1d invariant only governs the 'blocked' status, and quarantine is deliberately a different, recoverable status — so it is not a counterexample to 'every BLOCKED routes through block_task'. It IS a legitimately separate recovery channel with no resolver decision recorded; the unified-contract design should account for it as an explicit out-of-band operator-cleared pause, but the 'violates the invariant' framing is too strong.
findings.evidence: execute_phase.py:2695-2699 `await orch.plan_manager.update_task_status(task_id, "quarantined", meta={"blocked_reason": f"{prefix}: {exc}"})` — direct, no block_task/_maybe_resolve_blocker/resolve_blocker in the helper. Docstring 2676 `Idempotently stamps the task as quarantined (NOT blocked)`. Call sites at 2269 and 2606 catch `(AuthenticationFailedError, InfrastructureCircuitOpenError)` and route here. blocker_resolver.py:160-168 `if cls == fc.INFRA_CIRCUIT_OPEN: return _act("fall_through", ...)` exists but is reachable only if INFRA_CIRCUIT_OPEN is routed through resolve_blocker, which the quarantine helper does not do. CRITICAL NUANCE the finder mislabels: the SAME docstring (2686-2691) states `quarantined is non-terminal so Orchestrator.resume picks the task up automatically once the operator clears the underlying issue` and `block_reason_class is intentionally NOT stamped — a quarantined task is awaiting recovery, not classification`. So quarantine is a RESUMABLE pause, not a terminal blocked state.
findings.repro_or_probe: Trigger AuthenticationFailedError in a stub adapter and grep the ledger: a 'quarantined' status transition with NO blocker_escalated/resolution_chosen op, and on resume the task is re-picked-up (confirming non-terminal). Contrast with a SOFT_BLOCKER which routes through block_task and emits the resolver breadcrumb.

findings.title: Two independent turn-budget counters with no shared reset: a resolver escalate_budget/retry recovery cannot break the budget-tracker exhaustion trap
findings.claim: Confirmed. Once (task,role) is exhausted, delegate() short-circuits at 6504-6515 to the synthetic 'error_max_turns_escalation_exhausted' result, which (a) never reaches record_result (6654, after the early return) and (b) would not increment/reset there anyway since only the literal 'error_max_turns' subtype is handled. No reset() is called from execute_phase. The resolver's _resolver_retry (escalate_budget/retry_with_changes) resets only the TASK retry_count and re-enables the task; it does not reset the BudgetEscalationTracker. So a re-dispatched turn-exhausted task immediately re-exhausts at 6504, burning resolver cycles until max_cycles_per_blocker (3). The resolver's budget-escalation action class is therefore inert against the exact turn-exhaustion failure it targets — the two recovery budgets share no state.
findings.evidence: execute_phase.py:6455 `_budget_tracker = getattr(orch, "_budget_escalation_tracker", None)`. 6504-6515: `if _budget_tracker.is_exhausted(envelope.task_id, role): return AgentResult(..., subtype="error_max_turns_escalation_exhausted")` — early return BEFORE record_result. 6653-6654: `if _budget_tracker is not None and envelope.task_id: _budget_tracker.record_result(envelope.task_id, role, result.subtype)` — unreachable for the exhausted path because of the early return. budget_escalation.py:249-253: `if subtype == "error_max_turns": self._counters[key]+=1 else: self._counters.pop(key, None)` — only the literal 'error_max_turns' increments; the synthetic 'error_max_turns_escalation_exhausted' never reaches here. `grep -n '_budget_tracker.reset\|_budget_escalation_tracker.reset' execute_phase.py` -> NO hits (reset/reset_all at budget_escalation.py:269/277 are doc'd 'mainly useful for tests; not used in production'). _resolver_retry (1666-1673) sets `meta={"retry_count": 0, "resolver_action": "retry", "resolver_note": ...}` only — never touches _budget_escalation_tracker.
findings.repro_or_probe: Unit test: build an orchestrator whose _budget_escalation_tracker is pre-set to the exhausted count for (task,'developer'); call delegate twice — both return subtype='error_max_turns_escalation_exhausted', counter never decrements. Simulate _resolver_retry, then delegate a third time — assert it STILL short-circuits (no reset).

findings.title: In-memory resolver cycle-guard keys on the RAW failure_class while the ledger budget keys on the CLASSIFIED class — novel failures collapse to one 'unknown' ledger budget and resume-safety diverges
findings.claim: Confirmed. The in-memory per-process cycle guard (execute_phase.py:1836) keys on the RAW failure_class string, whereas resolve_blocker's resume-safe ledger budget (blocker_key, blocker_resolver.py:86) and count_prior_cycles key on the CLASSIFIED class. For novel failures (classify -> 'unknown'), the in-memory guard tracks each distinct raw string separately (3 cycles each) while the ledger folds all novel raw failures for a task into one '{task}:unknown' budget (3 total). The must-not-loop safety still holds (whichever budget is tighter bounds first within a process; the ledger budget is actually the tighter one for novel failures), but the two budgets disagree on blocker identity, making resume-safety accounting and post-mortems inconsistent for novel failures. Low blast radius.
findings.evidence: execute_phase.py:1836 `guard_key = f"{task.id if task is not None else '-'}:{failure_class}"` uses the RAW param. 1855 `fclass = _fc.classify(failure_class)`. ctx built with `failure_class=fclass` (1861) and recovery_already_tried=_prior_resolution_actions(orch, task_id, fclass) (1867, classified). blocker_resolver.py:79-86 blocker_key returns `f"{ctx.task_id or '-'}:{ctx.failure_class}"` (classified); used at 97 (count_prior_cycles) and 645 (the ledger breadcrumb key) and counted at 663. failure_classes.py:106-114 classify: returns raw unchanged only if in ALL_FAILURE_CLASSES, else UNKNOWN='unknown'. So two distinct raw strings both classifying to 'unknown' produce two distinct in-memory guard_keys but one shared ledger blocker_key '{task}:unknown'.
findings.repro_or_probe: Unit test: call _maybe_resolve_blocker twice with two DIFFERENT raw failure_class strings both classifying to UNKNOWN on the same task; assert orch._resolver_cycle_counts has two keys while the ledger resolution_chosen ops share blocker_key '{task}:unknown'.

findings.title: F1d AST invariant only catches update_task_status('blocked') call literals; direct task.status='blocked' assignments (cascade-block) are outside its scope, so its 'silent dead-end impossible by construction' claim is overstated
findings.claim: Confirmed. The F1d AST invariant only scans ast.Call to update_task_status with a 'blocked' constant; it cannot see attribute assignments. mark_blocked_descendants commits `t.status='blocked'` directly at plan_manager.py:1019 (live) and 1674 (replay), reaching terminal blocked for cascade-blocked dependents with NO blocker_escalated/resolution_chosen breadcrumb (only op=mark_blocked_descendants). The docstring's 'impossible to add by construction' guarantee is therefore true only for update_task_status-literal call sites — cascade-block is a real (defensible) exception, AND a future raw `task.status='blocked'` assignment anywhere would silently evade the gate. The invariant should also walk ast.Assign targeting attribute 'status' with Constant 'blocked' (forbid or whitelist) to make the guarantee real.
findings.evidence: test_block_path_invariant.py:57-77: _block_sites walks only `ast.Call` nodes (`if not isinstance(node, ast.Call): continue`) named update_task_status (66 `if name != "update_task_status": continue`) with a 'blocked' Constant arg/kwarg (69-74). ast.Assign nodes are never inspected. Module docstring 1-16 claims a task reaching terminal 'blocked' outside block_task — 'the Run-5 silent dead-end class' — is made 'impossible to add in future'. plan_manager.py:1019 `t.status = "blocked"  # type: ignore[assignment]` inside mark_blocked_descendants (live cascade-block), and :1674 the identical assignment in _apply_op replay (op=='mark_blocked_descendants'). The cascade emits `op="mark_blocked_descendants"` (1026), NOT blocker_escalated/resolution_chosen. Both confirmed via grep.
findings.repro_or_probe: Extend _block_sites() to also walk ast.Assign whose target is an ast.Attribute named 'status' and whose value is Constant 'blocked'; re-run pytest tests/test_block_path_invariant.py — it surfaces plan_manager.py:1019 and :1674 as currently-unguarded block sites.

findings.title: QA gates verify the WRONG tree: syntax/lint/build/test run on orch.cwd (main repo, pre-change) while the developer's diff lives only in the per-task worktree until after gates pass
findings.claim: Confirmed and slightly strengthened. In the parallel/git path (worktree_mgr set), the developer writes to the per-task worktree (cwd_override=worktree) but all QA gates run against orch.cwd (main repo) because _run_qa_gates hardcodes cwd=orch.cwd (:7514) and is invoked at :4538 with no worktree arg, while the diff is applied to main only later at :5349-5352. Refinement: lint/test DO receive diff-scoped `paths`, but since those paths point at files not yet materialized in main, new files are skipped (lint.py:106-108 'no changed python files present on disk') and modified files are gated against their PRE-change content — so even the scoped gates never see the candidate change. syntax_check/build_check ignore paths entirely and rglob the unchanged main tree. Net: a green gate-set proves nothing about the fix in the default parallel mode. Caveat: this is the _execute_one path; whether every deployment runs with worktree_mgr set (vs the serial cwd=orch.cwd path where gates and edits share the tree) determines field blast radius — worth confirming worktree_mgr is the production default before treating as universal.
findings.evidence: Read execute_phase.py:7513-7514 `cfg=orch.cfg.qa_gates; cwd=orch.cwd`; :7515 `language=detect_language(cwd)`. Gate dispatch :7575-7578 all build callables closing over this `cwd` (orch.cwd). _run_qa_gates def :7491-7495 has NO cwd_override param. Developer delegation :4374-4383 passes `cwd_override=worktree`; delegate :6572 `effective_cwd = cwd_override if cwd_override is not None else orch.cwd` and :6587 `cwd=effective_cwd` in AgentInvocation — so the LLM file edits land in the worktree. Gate call site :4538 `_run_qa_gates(orch, task, developer_result=...)` — no worktree arg. Apply ordering: gates at :4538 (Step 3), apply at :5349-5352 `if worktree_mgr is not None and worktree is not None: _apply_with_conflict_escalation(...)` (after Step 7), with comment :5341-5343 'apply the diff to the main repo BEFORE marking complete'. _apply_with_conflict_escalation :2086-2088 calls worktree_mgr.apply_patch_to_main. Test test_orchestrator_execute_phase_worktree.py:98-114 confirms the worktree file only appears in main AFTER apply_patch_to_main. So in the worktree_mgr path, syntax_check/build_check rglob orch.cwd (main, no candidate change); lint/test get diff-scoped paths but evaluate them against orch.cwd where new files are absent (lint.py:106-108 skips them) and modified files still hold OLD content.
findings.repro_or_probe: Integration test: init a git repo, run _execute_one with a real WorktreeManager and a developer stub whose diff introduces a syntax error into a tracked .py file in the worktree; assert run_syntax_check FAILS. With current code it passes because main is clean. Or assert that for a MODIFIED file, the gate sees pre-change content. Also confirm worktree_mgr is non-None in the standard execute path (it is created at :4281 create_per_task when worktree_mgr passed in).

findings.title: detect_language only inspects the literal repo root (non-recursive) -> monorepos with per-service manifests are classified None and ALL gates skip silently
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly as stated. detect_language is root-only/non-recursive; a monorepo whose manifests live only in subdirectories (services/api/go.mod, packages/x/package.json) returns None at root, so syntax/lint/build/test all hit the language-not-detected -> passed=True branch. Empirically reproduced: subdirectory-only go.mod -> detect_language=None. Zero build/test/lint/syntax verification for this common repo shape.
findings.evidence: Read detect.py:30-54: every check is root-only — `(cwd/'pyproject.toml').exists()`, `(cwd/'go.mod').exists()`, `list(cwd.glob('*.csproj'))` (glob = single level, not rglob), `(cwd/'CMakeLists.txt').exists()`, then `return None`. `grep -n rglob|os.walk` in detect.py returned nothing (0 hits). Empirical: created /tmp/monorepo_test/services/api/go.mod, ran detect_language -> printed None, is_repo_unbuildable -> True. Gate None-skip branches confirmed: test_runner.py:43-44, lint.py:39-40, build_check.py:35-36, syntax_check.py:35-36 all `if lang is None: return GateResult(passed=True, ...skipping)`.
findings.repro_or_probe: mkdir -p repo/services/api && touch repo/services/api/go.mod; detect_language(Path('repo')) -> None (verified). run_tests(repo) -> passed=True 'language not detected, skipping tests'.

findings.title: Two divergent language detectors disagree: qa/detect.py (manifest-first, root-only) vs runtime/language_profile.py (weighted file-extension scan)
findings.claim: Two independent primary-language resolvers exist with different algorithms and different answers (empirically: same Go+pyproject repo -> detect.py 'python' vs language_profile 'go'). The QA gates use the manifest-first root-only detect.py (execute_phase.py:7515); adapter/platform selection (adapters/detect.py:269-271), hallucination_guard, doctor, and init use the weighted-extension language_profile.py. The better signal exists but is thrown away at the gate boundary, with no reconciliation. Correction to the finder: the consumer is adapters/detect.py (not fitness.py — fitness.py:90 merely formats the profile dict into a warning string).
findings.evidence: Confirmed two distinct algorithms: detect.py:30-31 returns 'python' on a bare pyproject.toml (manifest-presence order, weakest signal first). language_profile.py:32-48 EXTENSION_WEIGHTS (.py weight 100, .go 50), :52 DOMINANT_THRESHOLD=0.40, :161-173 get_dominant_language returns share-weighted winner or 'mixed'. Gates use detect.py: execute_phase.py:7515 `language=detect_language(cwd)`. Empirical divergence reproduced: /tmp/dual_test with pyproject.toml + 9 .go files -> detect_language='python', get_dominant_language='go'. HOWEVER the finder's specific call-site cite is imprecise: fitness.py:90 only formats a profile dict for a warning string; it does NOT itself call compute_language_profile. The language_profile consumers are adapters/detect.py:269-271, qa/hallucination_guard.py:163-167, cli/commands/{execute,plan,doctor,init}.py. The 'adapters.fitness consumes from compute_language_profile' phrasing conflates fitness (pure formatter) with adapters/detect (the actual platform/adapter selector). Substance — two divergent detectors, gates trust the dumber root-only one, the smarter extension census exists but is not used at the gate boundary, no reconciliation — is fully correct.
findings.repro_or_probe: Repo of 90% .go + root pyproject.toml: detect_language(cwd)->'python', get_dominant_language(compute_language_profile(cwd))->'go' (verified at /tmp/dual_test). Decide which gates should trust.

findings.title: RegexExtractor tags ALL non-Py/TS/Cpp files lang='other', collapsing Go/Rust/Java/Ruby into one bucket -> file-index language filtering can never select them
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly as stated. Every language without a dedicated extractor (Go, Rust, Java, Ruby, C#, Swift, Kotlin, PHP) is stored with files.lang='other'. The file_index `languages` allowlist filters on this exact lang_tag, so languages={'go'} matches zero files and languages={'other'} returns an undifferentiated mix of every minority language. There is no way to scope retrieval to Go (or any regex-fallback language) by language.
findings.evidence: regex_extractor.py:47-48 `extensions=frozenset()` (claims nothing), `lang_tag='other'`. __init__.py:98-114 lookup_extractor returns the first EXTRACTORS member whose extensions contain the suffix, else RegexExtractor (lang_tag 'other'); dedicated extractors are py (py_extractor.py:32 lang_tag='py'), cpp (cpp_extractor.py:235 lang_tag='cpp'), and ts only — so .go/.rs/.java fall through to 'other' (empirically RegexExtractor().lang_tag printed 'other'). file_index.py:529 `lang=extractor.lang_tag` and :646 store lang_tag in files.lang. Filter at :992-996 `if languages is not None: allow=set(languages); parsed_iter=(p for p in parsed_iter if p.lang in allow)`. build_full docstring :918-920 lists valid lang_tag values as only ('py','cpp','ts','other').
findings.repro_or_probe: Index a Go repo, then IndexBuilder.build_full(cwd, db, languages=['go']) -> 0 files indexed (all Go files are lang='other'); languages=['other'] returns Go+Rust+Java+Ruby mixed. Assert file_count==0 for languages=['go'].

findings.title: cfg.index_languages is a documented config knob that is never read -- dead knob; and its only valid values are coarse lang_tags
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly. cfg.index_languages is declared in schema.py:1357 with a documented opt-in promise but has ZERO readers -- every IndexBuilder.build_full call site (plan.py:61, execute.py:58, resume.py:44) omits the `languages=` arg, so the knob is inert. It is doubly broken: even if wired, the file_index filter keys on lang_tags (py/cpp/ts/other per the docstring), so it could never select go/rust/java -- exactly the collapse from the prior finding.
findings.evidence: schema.py:1355-1357 `index_languages: list[str] | None = None` with docstring promising 'Pass an explicit list to opt-in to a subset, e.g. ["py"]'. `grep -rn index_languages src/ tests/ docs/` -> ONLY the schema.py:1357 declaration, zero readers. All three build_full call sites omit `languages=`: plan.py:61-63 `IndexBuilder.build_full(cwd, db_path, workers=workers, batch_size=batch_size)`, execute.py:58-60 same, resume.py:44-46 same. So cfg.index_languages is silently ignored. file_index.py:918-920 confirms even if wired the filter keys on lang_tag whose documented valid values are only py/cpp/ts/other -- cannot select 'go'/'rust'/'java'.
findings.repro_or_probe: Set cfg.index.index_languages=['py'], run a plan over a mixed repo; index still contains non-py files (knob ignored). grep build_full call sites to confirm no languages= threaded (verified: 0 of 3 pass it).

findings.title: Rust test gate is vacuous exactly like Go: cargo test on a crate with zero #[test] functions exits 0 -> silent pass
findings.claim: Confirmed by code-path parity (not subprocess-run). _run_cargo_test runs bare `cargo test` and passes on any rc==0; `cargo test` on a crate with no test targets exits 0 with 'running 0 tests'. So a Rust repo (or a changed crate) with no tests vacuously passes the test gate -- the same non-vacuity hole already flagged for Go (`go test ./...`) and pytest, but Rust was not separately called out. The non-vacuity fix is incomplete across first-class runnable languages until cargo/go/npm/pytest all assert tests-actually-ran.
findings.evidence: test_runner.py:125-126 `async def _run_cargo_test(cwd, *, timeout_s): return await _run_subprocess(['cargo','test'], cwd, timeout_s=timeout_s, tool_name='cargo test')` -- bare `cargo test`, no assertion that any test ran. _run_subprocess :91-92 `if proc.returncode == 0: return GateResult(passed=True, ...)`. This is structurally identical to _run_go_test :129-130 (`go test ./...`) which the seed already flagged as vacuous. The cargo behavior ('cargo test' with no #[test] -> 'running 0 tests; test result: ok' exit 0) is documented cargo behavior, not independently runnable here (no rust toolchain), but the CODE PATH (rc==0 -> pass, no non-vacuity check) is confirmed identical to the flagged Go hole.
findings.repro_or_probe: cargo new --lib foo; strip the default #[test]; `cargo test` -> 'running 0 tests; test result: ok' exit 0; run_tests(crate, language='rust') -> passed=True with 0 tests executed. (Requires rust toolchain; code path confirmed by read.)

findings.title: build_check and syntax_check are never diff-scoped (whole-tree rglob), unlike lint and test_runner which receive paths
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly. lint (:7576) and test_runner (:7578) receive diff-scoped paths; syntax_check (:7575) and build_check (:7577) are called with no paths and have no paths parameter, so _python_build/_python_syntax_check rglob the WHOLE tree (cwd.rglob('*.py')) every gate run. This is O(repo) per task at scale, cannot attribute a failure to the candidate diff, and a pre-existing unrelated syntax error in the tree fails the gate for an unrelated diff. It compounds the wrong-tree keystone (the two change-catching gates also scan the wrong, unchanged tree).
findings.evidence: execute_phase.py:7575 `('syntax_check', cfg.syntax_check, lambda: run_syntax_check(cwd, language))` and :7577 `('build_check', cfg.build_check, lambda: run_build_check(cwd, language))` -- NO paths kwarg. Contrast :7576 `run_lint(cwd, language, paths=secretscan_paths, ...)` and :7578 `run_tests(cwd, paths=secretscan_paths, ...)` -- paths passed. run_syntax_check signature (syntax_check.py:23-28) and run_build_check (build_check.py:23-28) have NO paths param at all. build_check.py:81-85 `py_files=[str(p) for p in cwd.rglob('*.py') if '.venv' not in p.parts ...]`; syntax_check.py:75 same `cwd.rglob('*.py')`. Both compile the entire main tree every gate run (bounded only by the ARG_MAX batcher syntax_check.py:46-65).
findings.repro_or_probe: Time run_syntax_check on a 5k-file tree vs a 3-file diff. Or add a pre-existing syntax error in an untouched file + a clean diff elsewhere -> gate blocks the clean diff, proving non-scoping.

findings.title: JS/Rust/Go test+lint+build gates silently ignore the paths diff-scope that the Python path honors
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly. run_tests/run_lint accept paths but thread it ONLY into the Python branch; the nodejs/rust/go runner helpers have signature (cwd,*,timeout_s) and drop paths, so npm test / cargo test / go test ./... / npx eslint . / cargo clippy / golangci-lint run / cargo check / go build ./... always run the whole suite/tree regardless of diff size. Python is privileged with diff-scoping; the other declared-first-class languages are second-class on both speed and failure-attribution, and a small TS/Go/Rust fix can blow the timeout (recorded as a FALSE block).
findings.evidence: test_runner.py:46-47 python branch `_run_pytest(cwd, timeout_s=timeout_s, paths=paths)` (paths threaded); :49-57 `runners={'nodejs':_run_npm_test,'rust':_run_cargo_test,'go':_run_go_test}; runner=runners.get(lang); return await runner(cwd, timeout_s=timeout_s)` -- paths DROPPED. Helper sigs :121 `_run_npm_test(cwd,*,timeout_s)`, :125 `_run_cargo_test(cwd,*,timeout_s)`, :129 `_run_go_test(cwd,*,timeout_s)` -- no paths param; argv is `npm test`/`cargo test`/`go test ./...` (whole suite). lint.py:42-43 python threads paths; :50-53 non-python runners get `(cwd, timeout_s=timeout_s)` only; helpers :113 `npx eslint .`, :118 `cargo clippy`, :122 `golangci-lint run` (all unscoped). build_check.py:38-47 only `_run_python_build` is path-relevant; rust/go helpers :133 `cargo check`, :137 `go build ./...` whole-tree.
findings.repro_or_probe: run_tests(cwd, language='go', paths=[Path('one_file.go')]) -> argv still `go test ./...` (paths ignored). run_lint(language='rust', paths=[...]) -> `cargo clippy` unscoped. Confirmed by code read; subprocess run needs toolchains.

findings.title: C++ is detected as first-class-indexed yet has NO build/test/lint/syntax runner, and its soft-pass net (is_repo_unbuildable) is unreachable on normal-sized repos
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly. detect_language returns 'cpp' (and C++ gets first-class tree-sitter symbol/secretscan treatment), but 'cpp' is in no gate runner dict, so all four gates return passed=True (verified: build/test/lint/syntax all 'skipping' on a CMake repo). The intended soft-pass net (is_repo_unbuildable -> treat_unrunnable_tests_as_no_tests) lives behind apply_huge_repo_profile's `if not is_huge_repo: return cfg` identity guard at :60-62, so on a normal-sized C++ repo the net at :65 is never reached AND no gate runs -- a fully green gate-set with zero compilation/test/lint and no 'not verified' disclosure. 'should' (not 'must') because cpp is by-design outside RUNNABLE_TEST_LANGUAGES; the defect is the unreachable net + absent small-repo signal.
findings.evidence: detect.py:50-53 returns 'cpp' for *.sln/*.vcxproj/CMakeLists.txt. RUNNABLE_TEST_LANGUAGES :99-108 excludes 'cpp'; is_repo_unbuildable :111-118 returns True for cpp. 'cpp' is in NO gate runner dict: build_check.py:38-43 runners={python,nodejs,rust,go}, :44-46 `runner=runners.get(lang); if runner is None: return GateResult(passed=True, ...skipping)`; same for test_runner.py:49-56, lint.py:45-52; syntax_check.py:42-43 falls to the 'no syntax checker' passed=True branch. huge_repo_profile.py:60-62 `if not is_huge_repo(cwd, cfg=cfg): return cfg` (identity) -- the is_repo_unbuildable->treat_unrunnable_tests override at :65 is only reached when is_huge_repo is True. Empirically: /tmp/cpp_test with CMakeLists.txt -> detect='cpp', is_repo_unbuildable=True, and run_build_check/run_tests/run_lint/run_syntax_check ALL returned passed=True with 'skipping' details.
findings.repro_or_probe: Small repo: CMakeLists.txt + a .cpp with a syntax error; run the full gate-set -> all passed=True (skipping) and is_repo_unbuildable's soft-pass never fires (is_huge_repo False). Verified gate behavior at /tmp/cpp_test.

findings.title: No ruff/mypy gate exists anywhere in CI or release — the north-star 'ruff/mypy green' is unenforced; src has 8 ruff + 34 mypy errors today
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly as stated. No CI/release workflow runs ruff, mypy, or any lint/type gate; pyproject declares mypy>=1.14 as an unused dev dep, has no ruff dep and no [tool.ruff]/[tool.mypy] config. Local run: 8 ruff errors in src/, 34 mypy errors across 16 files. The 'ruff/mypy green' north-star is unenforced by any gate.
findings.evidence: grep -rin 'ruff|mypy|lint|pyright' .github/workflows/ → no matches (all 3 workflows). test.yml steps confirmed: only 'Run tests' (uv run pytest tests/ -v, line 30), 'E2E with fake binaries' (33), 'Slash command template drift check' (36). release.yml:348-349 = 'Full pytest run' → 'uv run pytest tests/ -v' (sole test step). pyproject.toml line 57 = 'mypy>=1.14' (a dep, never invoked); grep -in 'ruff' pyproject.toml → no ruff anywhere; no [tool.ruff] / [tool.mypy] sections present (grep '[tool.' shows only hatch/pytest). Local: `ruff check src/` → 'Found 8 errors'; `uv run mypy src/` → 'Found 34 errors in 16 files (checked 158 source files)'.
findings.repro_or_probe: Confirmed: `ruff check src/` → 8 errors; `uv run mypy src/` → 34 errors/16 files; `grep -rin 'ruff\|mypy\|lint\|pyright' .github/workflows/` → empty.

findings.title: claude_code passes `--allowed-tools ""` to disable tools, but the Claude CLI does NOT treat an empty allow-list as no-tools — the correct flag is `--tools ""`; the unit test asserts the wrong incantation and is vacuously green
findings.claim: Confirmed: the adapter emits `--allowed-tools ''` for [], and the unit test is a vacuous string-equality assertion that proves the flag is emitted, not that the CLI honors it as no-tools. UNVERIFIED here (needs a live `claude` probe): the claim that the CLI ignores an empty `--allowed-tools` and that `--tools ''` is the correct disable flag. Treat the test-vacuity as confirmed; treat the wrong-flag/field-inertness as plausible-but-unconfirmed (consistent with Run-5/6 memory of A4 exhausting critic_t).
findings.evidence: claude_code.py:232-242 confirmed: `if inv.allowed_tools is not None:` then `cmd += ['--allowed-tools', ','.join(inv.allowed_tools)]`; ','.join([]) == '' so [] emits `--allowed-tools ''`. Test (lines 62-72) test_claude_empty_list_passes_empty_allow_list asserts ONLY `cmd[idx+1] == ''` -- a pure string-equality check that never spawns the CLI or verifies tools are disabled (vacuous w.r.t. runtime behavior): CONFIRMED. HOWEVER I cannot independently verify the central correctness claim -- that the live Claude CLI ignores `--allowed-tools ''` and that `--tools ''` is the right flag -- without running `claude --help`/a live probe, which I did not do. The adapter comment (235-241) explicitly claims `--allowed-tools ''` IS the empty allow-list and only critic_t/synthesizer reach it; the CLI-semantics rebuttal rests on the finder's reading of --help plus prior field memory, not on code I can check here.
findings.repro_or_probe: Live probe required: `claude -p 'list your tools' --allowed-tools ''` vs `claude -p 'list your tools' --tools ''` and observe tool availability; confirm via `claude --help` whether `--tools` documents 'Use "" to disable all tools'. Only then upgrade to must_fix; downgraded to should pending that empirical confirmation.

findings.title: The Universal Blocker Resolver (headline v0.42.x feature) is force-DISABLED by an autouse conftest fixture for the entire suite; only 3 of ~406 test files opt back in
findings.claim: Confirmed in substance: an autouse conftest fixture sets AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED=1 for every test except those marked @pytest.mark.resolver_enabled; only 3 real test files (test_execute_phase_resolver_wiring.py, test_resolver_engagement.py, test_specialist_role_dispatch.py) opt back in. record_phase_degrade is gated on the same kill-switch (blocker_resolver.py:747-754), so degrade-observability is also off across the suite. Denominator is 383 test_*.py files (finder said ~406), so the ratio is even starker — but production/CLI/benchmark do NOT set the env var, so the resolver is ON there (conftest docstring lines 32-33), which slightly tempers 'tests validate what ships'.
findings.evidence: conftest.py:16-38: autouse fixture _resolver_disabled_by_default; lines 35-38 `if request.node.get_closest_marker('resolver_enabled'): monkeypatch.delenv('AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED', raising=False) else: monkeypatch.setenv('AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED', '1')`. `grep -rln resolver_enabled tests` → exactly 4 files: conftest.py + test_execute_phase_resolver_wiring.py + test_resolver_engagement.py + test_specialist_role_dispatch.py (3 real test files opt in). blocker_resolver.py:747-754 record_phase_degrade early-returns when rcfg disabled OR AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED in ('1','true','yes'). Denominator correction: `ls tests/test_*.py | wc -l` = 383 (not ~406).
findings.repro_or_probe: `grep -rln resolver_enabled tests | wc -l` = 4 (incl conftest); `ls tests/test_*.py | wc -l` = 383. To quantify the hole: flip the conftest default to resolver-ON and run `uv run pytest tests/ -x`, counting failures.

findings.title: block_path_invariant guarantees only that IF a blocked transition is committed it goes through block_task — it does NOT guarantee block_task (and thus the resolver) is REACHED; alternate terminals (budget-exhaustion AgentResult, degrade) bypass it
findings.claim: Partial. The HIGH-LEVEL point is sound and confirmed: the AST invariant (test_block_path_invariant.py:80-90) proves block-commit UNIQUENESS, not that block_task / the resolver is ever REACHED, and choose_recovery_action is audit-only (5655-5660) -- so 'every terminal preceded by exactly one recovery decision' is not enforced by this test, and Run-6's '0 fires' is real field evidence. But the SPECIFIC cited bypass -- error_max_turns_escalation_exhausted at 6509 'a terminal that doesn't call block_task' -- is REFUTED: that AgentResult is an intermediate return inside delegate(); the enclosing retry ladder _try_retry_or_escalate routes exhaustion into block_task at 6053 (→ _maybe_resolve_blocker), and the F1e crash path (6602-6633) emits an escalation crumb. The gap is the absence of a positive engagement/reachability invariant, not these two specific terminals leaking past block_task.
findings.evidence: test_block_path_invariant.py:80-90 confirmed: scans only for `update_task_status(...,'blocked')` Call nodes outside (blocker_guard.py, block_task) -- it proves block-COMMIT uniqueness, not reachability/engagement. choose_recovery_action audit-only comment CONFIRMED at execute_phase.py:5655-5660 ('The action does not currently override the ladder's choice ... an audit-only annotation'). BUT the specific bypass mechanism cited is REFUTED: line 6509's `return AgentResult(..., subtype='error_max_turns_escalation_exhausted')` is inside `delegate()` (def at 6072) -- it is an INTERMEDIATE return value, not a terminal task state. The retry ladder `_try_retry_or_escalate()` (def at 5534) consumes exhaustion and DOES route through `block_task` at 6053 with failure_class=UNKNOWN, which the F1 chokepoint (block_task → block_hook=_maybe_resolve_blocker, registered at 2245-2251) feeds into the resolver. So that exhaustion path does NOT bypass block_task. Additionally, execute_phase.py:6602-6633 (F1e) emits a blocker_escalated crumb on raw-dispatch crash before re-raising -- another closed gap.
findings.repro_or_probe: To prove the residual gap, add a positive invariant: assert every success=False AgentResult reaching the phase boundary is preceded by a blocker_escalated op (or trace each terminal-return subtype to a block_task caller). Field-probe: a 4×-max-turns task; grep ledger for blocker_escalated (Run-6 showed 0). Downgraded from must_fix to should because the cited bypass mechanism is incorrect and the dominant exhaustion path provably routes through block_task.

findings.title: StubAdapter auto-returns success=True for every unstubbed role AND special-cases gate-pass verdicts (drift APPROVED, sounding_board approved, framing local_defect) — masking rejection/failure paths in ~20 tests
findings.claim: Confirmed exactly. Unstubbed roles default to success=True, and four safety-critical gate roles auto-return their PASS verdict (drift APPROVED, sounding_board approved-extended-scope, framing local_defect, altitude_judge valid ranking). 20 test files instantiate StubAdapter({}) relying on the fallback, so a test that forgets to stub a gate gets a silent auto-pass and 'pipeline completes' assertions stay green even when a rejecting gate never executed. Title's 'framing local_defect' matches src (line 103 CLASSIFICATION: local_defect; the 'local_patch' phrase in the comment is the downstream effect).
findings.evidence: stub_adapter.py confirmed line-by-line: 58-63 critic_drift_verifier→'VERDICT: APPROVED\n' (comment line 56-57 'mirrors ... the gate's safe-mode position'); 69-77 critic_sounding_board+EXTENDED_SCOPE_REVIEW→'RESOLUTION: approved-extended-scope'; 83-94 synthesizer+CANDIDATE 1→no-op merged diff; 98-110 framing→'CLASSIFICATION: local_defect'; 113-118 altitude_judge→'RANKING: 1 2 3'; 119-123 generic fallback `AgentResult(success=True, text=f'[stub:{inv.role}] default-ok')`. `grep -rln 'StubAdapter({})' tests | wc -l` = 20.
findings.repro_or_probe: Confirmed counts. To quantify masking: make the generic fallback (119-123) raise instead of returning default-ok, run the suite, count tests failing purely on an unstubbed gate auto-pass. Policy fix: no-default / explicit-stub-required for gate roles.

findings.title: Cursor adapter CANNOT enforce allowed_tools at all — text-only roles run with full tool access on Cursor; only a warning is logged. Adapter parity is broken for tool-scoping

Hard parity divergence from claude_code (which at least emits a flag). Not must_fix because claude_code is the default platform, but it violates WS-3 adapter parity and the safe-degrade promise (degrades silently without surfacing impact to run outcome).
findings.evidence: cursor.py:202-214 confirmed: `if inv.allowed_tools is not None:` → `logger.warning('cursor.allowed_tools_ignored', role=..., allowed_tools=..., note='cursor has no --allowed-tools ...')` then `return cmd` with NO tool-restriction flag added for ANY allowed_tools value (including [] no-tools and non-empty allow-lists). Comment 206-207: 'Cursor still cannot ENFORCE any allow-list (no --allowed-tools flag)'. Test test_cursor_empty_list_emits_warning (test_adapters_allowed_tools_scoping.py:80-103) asserts only the warning fires and `'--allowed-tools' not in cmd` — codifying non-enforcement as correct. _build_command signature (cursor.py:169) is (self, binary, inv); test calls `adapter._build_command('cursor', inv)` correctly.
findings.repro_or_probe: Orchestrator-level assertion: reject/degrade text-only roles on a non-enforcing adapter rather than silently run unscoped. Field probe: platform=cursor tournament with critic_t allowed_tools=[]; observe agent using Edit/Bash.

findings.title: The degrade-capable-phases invariant is a source SUBSTRING check ('record_phase_degrade(' in file text), proving presence not engagement; and the degrade breadcrumb itself is resolver-gated so it no-ops under the suite's default-disabled resolver

And record_phase_degrade itself early-returns (blocker_resolver.py:746-754) when the resolver is disabled or AUTODEV_RESOLVER_DISABLED is set -- the suite default and any field run with the resolver off -- so the 'makes silent degrade explicit' breadcrumb is itself silent in nearly all tests and in any resolver-off field run. (Cited line 744-752 → actual 746-754.)

findings.title: A4 ROOT CAUSE: `--allowed-tools ""` does NOT disable tools, so critic_t still does tool-driven file reads (190-209K tokens) → error_max_turns; v0.42.1 fixed the WRONG channel
findings.file_line: src/adapters/claude_code.py:232-242 (cmd build), src/tournament/llm.py:335-336 (role→[]), Run-6 field memory
findings.claim: The inline-prompt channel for critic_t is provably bounded (≤12000 chars ≈ 3K tokens via `_limit` at plan_tournament.py:86; CRITIC_PROMPT never instructs reads), so it cannot account for the field-observed 190-209K-token critic_t exhaustion — the bloat must come from a different channel. The adapter builds `--allowed-tools ""` (an empty allow-LIST) for critic_t/synthesizer alongside `--permission-mode acceptEdits`. The claim that this empty allow-list does NOT disable CLI tools (so the model autonomously reads files until error_max_turns) is consistent with the code but is attested only by Run-6 field memory, not provable from this repo; it requires an operator-gated real-CLI probe to confirm. Fix direction (use `--disallowed-tools` or a no-op sentinel, and assert 0 tool_use blocks) is valid: there is zero `--disallowed-tools` usage in the adapter.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED in code: claude_code.py:232-242 — `if inv.allowed_tools is not None:` then `cmd += ["--allowed-tools", ",".join(inv.allowed_tools)]`; for `[]`, `",".join([])==""` → literally `--allowed-tools ""`. claude_code.py:220-221 passes `--permission-mode acceptEdits`. tournament/llm.py:76 `_TEXT_ONLY_NO_TOOL_ROLES = frozenset({"critic_t","synthesizer"})` and llm.py:335-336 returns `[]` for those roles (precedence over the ['Read'] sentinel). prompts.py:27 CRITIC_PROMPT inlines only `{version_a}` (rendered via `_limit(t,12000)` at plan_tournament.py:86) and explicitly says 'Find real problems / Do NOT propose fixes' — it never instructs the model to read files. So inline content is ~12000 chars ≈ 3K tokens, provably NOT the 190K bloat. WHAT I COULD NOT INDEPENDENTLY PROVE FROM CODE: that the Claude CLI treats an empty `--allowed-tools ""` allow-list as 'all tools' rather than 'no tools', and that the model then autonomously reads 190-209K tokens of files burning 6-7 turns. There is no code or test in this repo that exercises a real CLI to demonstrate this; the num_turns=7 / stop_reason=tool_use figures come solely from Run-6 field memory (operator-attested), not from anything observable in HEAD. So the MECHANISM (inline channel is bounded and cannot be the bloat) is fully code-confirmed; the SPECIFIC CLI-semantics root cause is field-attested, not code-provable here. `grep -in disallowed src/adapters/claude_code.py` → empty (no --disallowed-tools usage), corroborating the fix-direction gap.
findings.repro_or_probe: Operator-gated field probe (the only way to settle the CLI-semantics sub-claim): `claude -p '<self-contained prompt referencing a 200KB file>' --permission-mode acceptEdits --max-turns 6 --allowed-tools "" --output-format json`; inspect JSON `num_turns`/`stop_reason` — expect tool_use turns + >100K tokens if the empty allow-list does not gate tools. Code probe (already run): `grep -in disallowed src/adapters/claude_code.py` → empty.

findings.title: No test or release gate asserts the critic actually runs tool-less — tests only check the FLAG VALUE `--allowed-tools ""`, not engagement
findings.claim: Confirmed verbatim: every A4-related assertion stops at the constructed command-line argument (`cmd[idx+1] == ""`) or the recorded invocation field (`c.allowed_tools == []`); none asserts that a spawned CLI actually performs zero tool reads for critic_t. This is a presence-not-engagement gate gap that let the empty-tools scoping ship green while the field still exhausts.
findings.evidence: test_adapters_allowed_tools_scoping.py:68-72 — `cmd = adapter._build_command(_make_inv(allowed_tools=[]))`; `assert "--allowed-tools" in cmd`; `assert cmd[idx+1] == ""` — pure argument-construction assertion, no spawned process. test_plan_tournament_runner_text_only_tools.py:211-216 asserts `c.allowed_tools == []` / `!= ["Read"]` on the INVOCATION OBJECT (a fake adapter records `c.allowed_tools`), never on a spawned CLI's behavior. ENGAGEMENT-NEGATIVE: `grep -rln 'critic_t' tests/ | xargs grep -ln 'num_turns\|tool_use'` → NO file matches (exit 1). All `num_turns`/`tool_use` occurrences in tests/test_adapter_claude.py (lines 49,323,325,376,378) are inside hand-written JSON returned by `create_subprocess_exec` mocks (every test at lines 75,91,107,... patches `adapters.claude_code.asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`), so they never exercise real CLI tool-gating. No test spawns a tool-capable CLI to assert critic_t emits 0 tool_use blocks.
findings.repro_or_probe: `pytest tests/test_adapters_allowed_tools_scoping.py -k empty` passes purely on flag value. Add a gate test that runs the real adapter against a tool-capable fake CLI (or the real CLI under an operator gate) and asserts the resulting JSON has no `tool_use` block / `num_turns==1` for critic_t. Severity lowered to 'should': it is a real gate gap but is the test-side mirror of finding #1's still-unproven root cause — not independently release-blocking until the CLI-semantics root cause is confirmed.

findings.title: repo_probe shape signals avg_file_size_bytes / largest_dir / largest_dir_file_count / depth_max are DEAD: computed, logged, stored — never read by any gate
findings.file_line: src/runtime/repo_probe.py:287-308 (computed/stored), grep of src/ for `.avg_file_size_bytes`/`.largest_dir`/`.depth_max` = 0 hits

The only consumed scale field is the coarse binary `is_huge` (file_count>20K OR total_bytes>5GB). No large-file or deep-tree gate exists, so a repo with one giant file is invisible to scale handling.

findings.title: `is_huge` is binary (file_count>20K OR bytes>5GB) and tournament critic/synthesizer/judge turns do NOT scale with it — so huge-repo handling never adjusts the bloat-prone critic budget
findings.claim: Confirmed: `resolve_task_max_turns`'s is_huge multiplier (task_overrides.py:100) scales only DEVELOPER/task agents via TASK_MAX_TURNS_DEFAULTS; tournament roles get a flat `spec.max_turns or 1` (plan_tournament_runner.py:125) resolved by `_resolve_max_turns(role)` (llm.py:311-314), which takes no capacity argument. So on huge repos the critic budget is NOT bumped while files are larger, and the binary is_huge gives no gradation — compounding the A4 exhaustion at scale. (Note: this assumes finding #1's tool-read root cause; if tools are properly disabled, a larger critic budget would not matter since the inline content is already bounded.)
findings.evidence: repo_probe.py:43-44 `_HUGE_FILE_COUNT_THRESHOLD = 20_000` / `_HUGE_TOTAL_BYTES_THRESHOLD = 5 * 1024**3`; :279-282 `is_huge = (file_count > _HUGE_FILE_COUNT_THRESHOLD or total_bytes > _HUGE_TOTAL_BYTES_THRESHOLD)` — pure binary OR. llm.py:311-314 `_resolve_max_turns(self, role)` returns `self._role_max_turns.get(role, 1)` — a flat per-role map, NO capacity/is_huge argument. plan_tournament_runner.py:125 `role_max_turns[role] = spec.max_turns or 1` (no capacity). task_overrides.py:95-100 `resolve_task_max_turns`: `if task.complexity is None: return None` then the is_huge multiplier at :100 (`if capacity is not None and capacity.is_huge:`) applies only to `TASK_MAX_TURNS_DEFAULTS` (developer task buckets), never to critic_t/synthesizer/judge. Independent grep `grep -rn role_max_turns|_resolve_max_turns|_role_max_turns ... | grep -i 'capacity|is_huge'` → EMPTY (exit 1): no capacity ever flows into tournament role budgets.
findings.repro_or_probe: `grep -n 'capacity\|is_huge\|resolve_task_max_turns' src/tournament/llm.py` → only `_resolve_max_turns` (role-only). Trace `_build_role_overrides` (plan_tournament_runner.py:85-154): no capacity/is_huge reference; budgets are `spec.max_turns or 1`.

findings.title: v0.42.1 PARTIALLY fixed inline-bloat: plan-tournament prompts ARE now render-bounded (real fix) — but impl/phase-review already had it, and none of it addresses tool reads
findings.claim: Confirmed: v0.42.1 (commit d7758b3, util._limit hoist) genuinely added 12000/8000-char render bounds to the plan-tournament critic/architect_b/synthesizer/judge renders (previously unbounded — the Run-5 inline root cause); impl_tournament and phase_review already bounded their diffs at 12000 pre-v0.42.1. The inline-prompt channel is now scoped everywhere. `_limit` cannot reach the tool-read channel of finding #1. This correctly de-stales the seed's 'unimplemented' framing for the inline half.
findings.evidence: plan_tournament.py:86 `return CRITIC_PROMPT.format(version_a=_limit(t, 12000))`; :97-99 architect_b bounds task_prompt/version_a/critic each at 12000; :110-112 synthesizer bounds at 8000; :132-135,142 judge bounds at 8000. util.py:3-8 docstring states the hoist is v0.42.1 (F2/A4) and that 'the unbounded plan text fed to critic / architect_b / synthesizer / judge was the root cause of the Run-5 critic_t error_max_turns exhaustion (190K–262K-token reads)'. `git log --oneline -- src/tournament/util.py` → `d7758b3 fix(tournament): bound plan-tournament render inputs (A4) + hoist _limit` (single commit, the v0.42.1 fix). Pre-existing bounds: impl_tournament.py:287 `diff=_limit(t.diff, 12000)` (plus 291/301/317/322/349/380); phase_review.py:263 `diff=_limit(t.diff, 12000)` (plus 281/435). So the inline channel is bounded everywhere; the tool-read channel (finding #1) is untouched by `_limit`.
findings.repro_or_probe: `git log -1 --format=%H -- src/tournament/util.py` → d7758b3; `grep -n '_limit' src/tournament/plan_tournament.py` shows live bounding. Severity 'nice' (down from should): this is a correction that prevents a redundant fix, not itself a defect to fix.

findings.title: phase-review & impl bundles store the FULL unbounded diff in memory; only the prompt RENDER is head-truncated — a defect past char 12000 of a large diff is never shown to the critic
findings.claim: Confirmed: the full diff is stored unbounded in PhaseReviewBundle.diff (phase_review_runner.py:304) and ImplBundle.diff (impl_tournament_runner.py:322); truncation happens only at render via `_limit(t.diff, 12000)` (phase_review.py:263 / impl_tournament.py:287), and `_limit` is head-only `text[:limit]` (util.py:18-20). Two consequences: (a) the whole diff string is materialized in the orchestrator process before truncation (memory/scale hazard on very large diffs), and (b) a defect living past char 12000 of a large diff is silently absent from the critic prompt — weakening review exactly on the large-change cases.
findings.evidence: phase_review_runner.py:293 `diff_text = _git_diff_range(orch.cwd, baseline_commit, tip_commit) or ""` (whole diff materialized); :304 `diff=diff_text` stored unbounded in PhaseReviewBundle. Truncation is render-only: phase_review.py:263 `diff=_limit(t.diff, 12000)`. `_limit` (util.py:14-20) is head-only: `if len(text) <= limit: return text; return text[:limit] + f"\n... (truncated {len(text) - limit} bytes)"` — no diff-aware/hunk-aware selection, so a defect in a hunk past char 12000 is dropped from the critic prompt. Impl side mirrors: impl_tournament_runner.py:322 `diff=diff` stored whole; impl_tournament.py:287 `diff=_limit(t.diff, 12000)` truncates only at render. CONFIRMED head-only + full-store on both paths.
findings.repro_or_probe: Build a PhaseReviewBundle whose diff has a clean first 12KB and a broken hunk at char 20000; call render_for_critic and assert the broken hunk is absent from the rendered prompt (demonstrates the blind spot). A hunk-aware or defect-region-prioritizing truncation would fix it.

findings.title: ZERO monorepo/workspace-member resolution anywhere — detect_language is root-only first-match-wins; polyglot/workspace repos get the wrong gate set
findings.file_line: src/qa/detect.py:30-54; consumed at src/orchestrator/execute_phase.py:7515 and re-detected in build_check.py:34, test_runner.py:42, lint.py:38, syntax_check.py:34

No Yarn/pnpm/npm-workspace, Cargo [workspace], Gradle multi-module, or Nx/Turbo/Lerna handling exists anywhere in src/. detect_language inspects only the literal repo root (cwd=orch.cwd) with first-match-wins ordering, so a root-pyproject.toml + services/api-go service resolves to 'python' and the Go service's tests are never run. get_dominant_language never drives gate language.
